units.translation: This seizer, by sea and by land.

τῶν πρόμαρπτι κάμνοις [may you perish before them, seizer], with the scholium πρότερον θάνοις, ὦ μάρπτι, πρὶν ἡμᾶς συλλαβεῖν [may you die first, seizer, before seizing us]: hence Hermannus proposed τῶν πρὸ σὺ, μάρπτι, κάμνοις [may you perish before them, seizer].
This dust bears witness for me.
Bear witness together, tracking the trail of evils.
Bear witness for me in death to this.
This cloak bears witness for me.
And to bear witness for me.
And I came to bear witness.
And it bears witness for me.
He himself was the one bearing witness.
Bearing witness to a deep fall for me.
For I am persuaded by these testimonies.
But you are called testimonies and proofs.
But from Zeus there were clear testimonies.
I call upon you to hear these things.
of the Sun: so that he may be present as my witness in the trial.
The child of Olympian Zeus is present as a witness.
Ares does not judge these things by witnesses.
Masistres (Persian proper name, first syllable long)
Persian proper name, first syllable long
The longer life, if it is extended further.
Inclining toward the greater of evils.
And now why need I tell you the greater things?

Do not care for me more than is sweet to me, where Elmsley rightly corrected to μασσόνως ἢ μοί [more than to me], on which see Hermann's note. Similar is μειζόνως [more greatly], which Euripides and other old Attic writers said, and μεζόνως [more greatly] in Herodotus.

O Zeus, the wrath of Io, investigator from the gods. The reading is corrupt, for which μαστίκτειρ' [flagellating] should be restored, as I showed above with Hartung on p. 166, which the scholiast seems to have read, explaining it as μαστιγωτική [scourging].
To Hermes, greatest patron and investigator.
The heavy, very heavy cold of the destructive public flagellator is present.
I am driven by the divine whip, goaded by the gadfly, from land to land.
Struck by the all-common whip of the god, he was subdued.
With a double whip, which Ares loves.

On the triple spelling μαζός μασθός [breast] and μαστός [breast], which the Attics constantly used, see Thes. vol. 5 p. 496 and 608. Correctly written in M Ch. 897 τόνδε δ' αἴδεσαι, τέκνον, μαστόν [respect this breast, child].
She attached the breast (thus Blomfield for μαζόν) in the dream.
She gaped around my nourishing breast (thus Blomfield for μασθόν).
Wolves carry the fawn under their armpits.
